update_log: Exhaustive compilation of 19th and 20th-century socio-religious reform movements in India, categorized by religion and caste reform for History Static GK.

hindu_reform_movements.key_objectives: Eradication of Sati, purdah system, and child marriage. Promoted monotheism and opposed idol worship. Later split into Adi Brahmo Samaj (Debendranath Tagore) and Brahmo Samaj of India (Keshub Chandra Sen).

Revival of the Vedas with the slogan 'Go back to the Vedas'. Opposed untouchability, polytheism, and idolatry. Started the 'Shuddhi Movement' to reconvert people to Hinduism. (Key Book: Satyarth Prakash).
Based on the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa. Focused on humanitarian relief, social work, and the Vedantic ideal that 'Service to man is service to God'.
Heavily influenced by the Brahmo Samaj. Focused on social reforms like widow remarriage, women's education, and abolition of the caste system. M.G. Ranade was its most prominent leader.

hindu_reform_movements.founder: Madam H.P. Blavatsky and Col. H.S. Olcott
hindu_reform_movements.key_objectives: Promoted universal brotherhood and the study of ancient Hindu, Zoroastrian, and Buddhist philosophies. Annie Besant later became its most famous leader in India.
A radical intellectual movement among students of Hindu College. Promoted rational thinking, free speech, and questioning of all religious and social orthodoxies.

caste_based_and_lower_caste_movements.key_objectives: Aimed to secure human rights and social justice for low-caste people and women. Strongly anti-Brahminical. (Key Book: Gulamgiri).

caste_based_and_lower_caste_movements.movement_name: SNDP Yogam (Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam)
caste_based_and_lower_caste_movements.key_objectives: Aimed at the spiritual and social upliftment of the depressed Ezhava community. Famous for the slogan: 'One religion, one caste, one God for mankind'.
Aimed at achieving equal rights for the non-Brahmin castes, promoting rationalism, opposing the caste system, and advocating for women's rights.
Formed for the moral and material progress of the untouchables. Slogan: 'Educate, Agitate, Organize'.
Founded to eradicate untouchability in India, working for the upliftment of Depressed Classes whom Gandhi called 'Harijans' (Children of God).

muslim_reform_movements.key_objectives: Aimed at the social, political, and educational upliftment of Indian Muslims through modern Western education. Founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College (now Aligarh Muslim University).

muslim_reform_movements.founder: Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi
muslim_reform_movements.key_objectives: An orthodox Islamic revivalist movement. Opposed the Aligarh movement's Westernization and focused on traditional Islamic scholarship. It also actively supported the Indian National Congress against the British.
Described itself as the standard-bearer of a true, liberal Islam. It promoted universal religion of all humanity and opposed Jihad as a sacred war.

sikh_and_parsi_reform_movements.founder: Thakur Singh Sandhawalia and Giani Gian Singh
sikh_and_parsi_reform_movements.key_objectives: Aimed to restore the purity of Sikhism, counter Christian missionary activities and Hindu revivalists, and promote modern education among Sikhs (led to the founding of Khalsa College).
An offshoot of the Singh Sabha Movement. Aimed to liberate Sikh Gurdwaras from the control of corrupt Udasin Mahants (priests). Resulted in the Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925.

sikh_and_parsi_reform_movements.founder: Naoroji Furdonji, Dadabhai Naoroji, S.S. Bengalee
sikh_and_parsi_reform_movements.key_objectives: Aimed at the regeneration of the social condition of the Parsis and the restoration of the Zoroastrian religion to its pristine purity. (Key Journal: Rast Goftar).
